exposure: racial/ethnic group (non-Hispanic Black vs. non-Hispanic White)
outcome: reasons for cesarean delivery (e.g., fetal intolerance of labor)
door-to-delivery time for unscheduled NTSV cesarean deliveries
cohort: The study participants were 31,826 nulliparous individuals with term singleton vertex births from 11 medical centers in North Carolina between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2021.
finding: Non-Hispanic Black patients were more likely to have an NTSV cesarean delivery and had shorter door-to-delivery times for unscheduled cesareans compared to non-Hispanic White patients, with fetal intolerance of labor being a more common reason for cesarean in Black patients.
mod_finding: Non-Hispanic Black individuals experienced higher rates of NTSV cesarean delivery and had faster decision-to-delivery times for unscheduled cesareans compared to non-Hispanic White individuals, with fetal intolerance of labor disproportionately cited as a reason.
